items.name: Montreal Game Jam Test
items.description:
The Montreal Game Jam was once one of the largest Game Jams in person, but since Covid this event was paused. 

In order to bring this event back, Conjure organized a free test Game Jam with a reduced number of participants.

This new version of the Montreal Game Jam de Conjure offers:

New format of theme and challenges
Game Jam in Lan format, all participants are grouped in the same room

A huge thank you to all the participants of the Montreal Game Jam Test. This edition marked the return of this event and we are delighted to have brought together so many passionate video game talents.

Students from several video game clubs from Montreal universities took up the challenge by creating apocalypse-themed games in less than three days!

A special thank you to our great organizing team: Ader Alisma, Chris Mathevet, Laura Bascopé Butron, Maurice Elkouby and Romain Boade whose work has made this event a real success.

Thank you to the School of Advanced Technology (ETS), which allowed us to use classroom facilities so that participants could work on their games in good conditions.

A big thank you to our sponsor Ubisoft Montreal, who offered prizes to our big winners.

You can now discover and play games created during Game Jam here: https://lnkd.in/eDjsTxXr

items.name: Student Game Dev Summit (1st edition)
items.location: ÉTS, Pavillon E, Salle des diplômés
items.description:
The Student Game Dev Summit is an event jointly organized by GameDev McGill, Concordia Game Development, Nad C.U.B.E, CJD - Université Laval and Conjure.

This evening allows members of the various video game creation clubs in Montreal and the surrounding area to meet, exchange and especially discover the games developed by the students. 

Beyond the projects presented, this event marks the beginning of a sustainable collaboration between the student communities in game development in the region. 

A huge thank you to the École de technologie supérieure (ETS) for welcoming us to the Graduate Fair for this first edition.

Also thank you to Loïc Beaudin-Kerzérho and Soro Nahouo Ouodio Abdul-Rahim from the ETS Exutoire club and to Tommy Cao for the photos and their contribution to the event.
